title: Unreachable code.
summary: Used when there is some code behind a "return" or "raise" statement, which will never be accessed. pylint calls it unreachable.

title: Dangerous default value … as argument.
summary: Used when a mutable value as list or dictionary is detected in a default value for an argument. pylint calls it dangerous-default-value.

title: Statement seems to have no effect.
summary: Used when a statement doesn't have (or at least seems to) any effect. pylint calls it pointless-statement.
message_templates: Statement seems to have no effect

title: String statement has no effect.
summary: Used when a string is used as a statement (which of course has no effect). This is a particular case of W0104 with its own message so you can easily disable it if you're using those strings as documentation, instead of comments. pylint calls it pointless-string-statement.

title: Expression "…" is assigned to nothing.
summary: Used when an expression that is not a function call is assigned to nothing. Probably something else was intended. pylint calls it expression-not-assigned.

title: Unnecessary pass statement.
summary: Used when a "pass" statement can be removed without affecting the behaviour of the code. pylint calls it unnecessary-pass.

title: Lambda may not be necessary.
summary: Used when the body of a lambda expression is a function call on the same argument list as the lambda itself; such lambda expressions are in all but a few cases replaceable with the function being called in the body of the lambda. pylint calls it unnecessary-lambda.

title: Duplicate key … in dictionary.
summary: Used when a dictionary expression binds the same key multiple times. pylint calls it duplicate-key.

title: Else clause on loop without a break statement, remove the else and de-indent all the code inside it.
summary: Loops should only have an else clause if they can exit early with a break statement, otherwise the statements under else should be on the same scope as the loop itself. pylint calls it useless-else-on-loop.
message_templates: Else clause on loop without a break statement, remove the else and de-indent all the code inside it

title: Use of exec.
summary: Raised when the 'exec' statement is used. It's dangerous to use this function for a user input, and it's also slower than actual code in general. This doesn't mean you should never use it, but you should consider alternatives first and restrict the functions available. pylint calls it exec-used.

title: Use of eval.
summary: Used when you use the "eval" function, to discourage its usage. Consider using ast.literal_eval for safely evaluating strings containing Python expressions from untrusted sources. pylint calls it eval-used.

title: Following "as" with another context manager looks like a tuple.
summary: Emitted when a with statement component returns multiple values and uses name binding with as only for a part of those values, as in with ctx() as a, b. This can be misleading, since it's not clear if the context manager returns a tuple or if the node without a name binding is another context manager. pylint calls it confusing-with-statement.
message_templates: Following "as" with another context manager looks like a tuple.

title: Using a conditional statement with a constant value.
summary: Emitted when a conditional statement (If or ternary if) uses a constant value for its test. This might not be what the user intended to do. pylint calls it using-constant-test.
message_templates: Using a conditional statement with a constant value

title: Using a conditional statement with potentially wrong function or method call due to missing parentheses.
summary: Emitted when a conditional statement (If or ternary if) seems to wrongly call a function due to missing parentheses. pylint calls it missing-parentheses-for-call-in-test.
message_templates: Using a conditional statement with potentially wrong function or method call due to missing parentheses

title: Assigning the same variable … to itself.
summary: Emitted when we detect that a variable is assigned to itself. pylint calls it self-assigning-variable.
message_templates: Assigning the same variable {} to itself

title: Redeclared variable … in assignment.
summary: Emitted when we detect that a variable was redeclared in the same assignment. pylint calls it redeclared-assigned-name.

title: Assert statement has a string literal as its first argument. The assert will … fail.
summary: Used when an assert statement has a string literal as its first argument, which will cause the assert to always pass. pylint calls it assert-on-string-literal.
message_templates: Assert statement has a string literal as its first argument. The assert will {} fail.

title: Duplicate value … in set.
summary: This message is emitted when a set contains the same value two or more times. pylint calls it duplicate-value.

title: Named expression used without context.
summary: Emitted if named expression is used to do a regular assignment outside a context like if, for, while, or a comprehension. pylint calls it named-expr-without-context.

title: Exception statement has no effect.
summary: Used when an exception is created without being assigned, raised or returned for subsequent use elsewhere. pylint calls it pointless-exception-statement.

title: 'return' shadowed by the 'finally' clause.
summary: Emitted when a 'return' statement is found in a 'finally' block. This will overwrite the return value of a function and should be avoided. pylint calls it return-in-finally.

title: The context used in function … will not be exited.
summary: Used when a contextmanager is used inside a generator function and the cleanup is not handled. pylint calls it contextmanager-generator-missing-cleanup.
message_templates: The context used in function {} will not be exited.

title: 'continue' discouraged inside 'finally' clause.
summary: Emitted when the continue keyword is found inside a finally clause. This will raise a SyntaxWarning starting in Python 3.14. pylint calls it continue-in-finally.

title: 'break' discouraged inside 'finally' clause.
summary: Emitted when the break keyword is found inside a finally clause. This will raise a SyntaxWarning starting in Python 3.14. pylint calls it break-in-finally.

title: Comparing against a callable, did you omit the parenthesis?.
summary: This message is emitted when pylint detects that a comparison with a callable was made, which might suggest that some parenthesis were omitted, resulting in potential unwanted behaviour. pylint calls it comparison-with-callable.
message_templates: Comparing against a callable, did you omit the parenthesis?

title: … statement in finally block may swallow exception.
summary: Used when a break or a return statement is found inside the finally clause of a try...finally block: the exceptions raised in the try clause will be silently swallowed instead of being re-raised. pylint calls it lost-exception.
message_templates: {} statement in finally block may swallow exception

title: Comparison … should be ….
summary: Used when an expression is compared to NaN values like math.nan, numpy.nan or float('nan'). pylint calls it nan-comparison.

title: Assert called on a populated tuple. Did you mean 'assert x,y'?.
summary: A call of assert on a tuple will always evaluate to true if the tuple is not empty, and will always evaluate to false if it is. pylint calls it assert-on-tuple.
message_templates: Assert called on a populated tuple. Did you mean 'assert x,y'?

title: Attribute … defined outside __init__.
summary: Used when an instance attribute is defined outside the __init__ method. pylint calls it attribute-defined-outside-init.

title: Static method with … as first argument.
summary: Used when a static method has "self" or a value specified in valid-classmethod-first-arg option or valid-metaclass-classmethod-first-arg option as first argument. pylint calls it bad-staticmethod-argument.
message_templates: Static method with {} as first argument

title: Access to a protected member … of a client class.
summary: Used when a protected member (i.e. class member with a name beginning with an underscore) is accessed outside the class or a descendant of the class where it's defined. pylint calls it protected-access.
message_templates: Access to a protected member {} of a client class

title: Flag member … shares bit positions with ….
summary: Used when multiple integer values declared within an enum.IntFlag class share a common bit position. pylint calls it implicit-flag-alias.
message_templates: Flag member {} shares bit positions with {}

title: … … … method.
summary: Used when a method has a different number of arguments than in the implemented interface or in an overridden method. Extra arguments with default values are ignored. pylint calls it arguments-differ.

title: Signature differs from … … method.
summary: Used when a method signature is different than in the implemented interface or in an overridden method. pylint calls it signature-differs.

title: Method … is abstract in class … but is not overridden in child class ….
summary: Used when an abstract method (i.e. raise NotImplementedError) is not overridden in concrete class. pylint calls it abstract-method.
message_templates: Method {} is abstract in class {} but is not overridden in child class {}

title: __init__ method from base class … is not called.
summary: Used when an ancestor class method has an __init__ method which is not called by a derived class. pylint calls it super-init-not-called.
message_templates: __init__ method from base class {} is not called

title: __init__ method from a non direct base class … is called.
summary: Used when an __init__ method is called on a class which is not in the direct ancestors for the analysed class. pylint calls it non-parent-init-called.
message_templates: __init__ method from a non direct base class {} is called

title: Method … was expected to be …, found it instead as ….
summary: Used when we detect that a method was overridden in a way that does not match its base class which could result in potential bugs at runtime. pylint calls it invalid-overridden-method.
message_templates: Method {} was expected to be {}, found it instead as {}

title: … … … method.
summary: Used when a method parameter has a different name than in the implemented interface or in an overridden method. pylint calls it arguments-renamed.

title: Unused private member `….…`.
summary: Emitted when a private member of a class is defined but not used. pylint calls it unused-private-member.

title: Method … overrides a method decorated with typing.final which is defined in class ….
summary: Used when a method decorated with typing.final has been overridden. pylint calls it overridden-final-method.
message_templates: Method {} overrides a method decorated with typing.final which is defined in class {}

title: Class … is a subclass of a class decorated with typing.final: ….
summary: Used when a class decorated with typing.final has been subclassed. pylint calls it subclassed-final-class.
message_templates: Class {} is a subclass of a class decorated with typing.final: {}

title: Redefined slots … in subclass.
summary: Used when a slot is re-defined in a subclass. pylint calls it redefined-slots-in-subclass.

title: Super call without brackets.
summary: Used when a call to super does not have brackets and thus is not an actual call and does not work as expected. pylint calls it super-without-brackets.

title: Useless parent or super() delegation in method ….
summary: Used whenever we can detect that an overridden method is useless, relying on parent or super() delegation to do the same thing as another method from the MRO. pylint calls it useless-parent-delegation.
message_templates: Useless parent or super() delegation in method {}

title: Unnecessary semicolon.
summary: Used when a statement is ended by a semi-colon (";"), which isn't necessary (that's python, not C ;). pylint calls it unnecessary-semicolon.

title: Bad indentation. Found … …, expected ….
summary: Used when an unexpected number of indentation's tabulations or spaces has been found. pylint calls it bad-indentation.

title: Wildcard import ….
summary: Used when from module import * is detected. pylint calls it wildcard-import.

title: Reimport … (imported line …).
summary: Used when a module is imported more than once. pylint calls it reimported.

title: Module import itself.
summary: Used when a module is importing itself. pylint calls it import-self.

title: Prefer importing … instead of ….
summary: Used when a module imported has a preferred replacement module. pylint calls it preferred-module.

title: __future__ import is not the first non docstring statement.
summary: Python 2.5 and greater require __future__ import to be the first non docstring statement in the module. pylint calls it misplaced-future.
message_templates: __future__ import is not the first non docstring statement

title: Shadowed … (imported line …).
summary: Used when a module is aliased with a name that shadows another import. pylint calls it shadowed-import.

title: Global variable … undefined at the module level.
summary: Used when a variable is defined through the "global" statement but the variable is not defined in the module scope. pylint calls it global-variable-undefined.
message_templates: Global variable {} undefined at the module level

title: Using global for … but no assignment is done.
summary: When a variable defined in the global scope is modified in an inner scope, the 'global' keyword is required in the inner scope only if there is an assignment operation done in the inner scope. pylint calls it global-variable-not-assigned.
message_templates: Using global for {} but no assignment is done

title: Using the global statement.
summary: Used when you use the "global" statement to update a global variable. Pylint discourages its usage. That doesn't mean you cannot use it!. pylint calls it global-statement.

title: Using the global statement at the module level.
summary: Used when you use the "global" statement at the module level since it has no effect. pylint calls it global-at-module-level.
message_templates: Using the global statement at the module level

title: Unused ….
summary: Used when an imported module or variable is not used. pylint calls it unused-import.

title: Unused variable ….
summary: Used when a variable is defined but not used. pylint calls it unused-variable.

title: Unused argument ….
summary: Used when a function or method argument is not used. pylint calls it unused-argument.

title: Unused import(s) … from wildcard import of ….
summary: Used when an imported module or variable is not used from a 'from X import *' style import. pylint calls it unused-wildcard-import.
message_templates: Unused import(s) {} from wildcard import of {}

title: Redefining name … from outer scope (line …).
summary: Used when a variable's name hides a name defined in an outer scope or except handler. pylint calls it redefined-outer-name.

title: Redefining built-in ….
summary: Used when a variable or function override a built-in. pylint calls it redefined-builtin.

title: Using possibly undefined loop variable ….
summary: Used when a loop variable (i.e. defined by a for loop or a list comprehension or a generator expression) is used outside the loop. pylint calls it undefined-loop-variable.

title: Possible unbalanced tuple unpacking with sequence …: left side has … label…, right side has … value….
summary: Used when there is an unbalanced tuple unpacking in assignment. pylint calls it unbalanced-tuple-unpacking.
message_templates: Possible unbalanced tuple unpacking with sequence {}: left side has {} label{}, right side has {} value{}

title: Cell variable … defined in loop.
summary: A variable used in a closure is defined in a loop. This will result in all closures using the same value for the closed-over variable. pylint calls it cell-var-from-loop.

title: Possibly unused variable ….
summary: Used when a variable is defined but might not be used. The possibility comes from the fact that locals() might be used, which could consume or not the said variable. pylint calls it possibly-unused-variable.

title: Invalid assignment to … in method.
summary: Invalid assignment to self or cls in instance or class method respectively. pylint calls it self-cls-assignment.

title: Possible unbalanced dict unpacking with …: left side has … label…, right side has … value….
summary: Used when there is an unbalanced dict unpacking in assignment or for loop. pylint calls it unbalanced-dict-unpacking.
message_templates: Possible unbalanced dict unpacking with {}: left side has {} label{}, right side has {} value{}

title: No exception type(s) specified.
summary: A bare except: clause will catch SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt exceptions, making it harder to interrupt a program with Control-C, and can disguise other problems. If you want to catch all exceptions that signal program errors, use except Exception: (bare except is equivalent to except BaseException:). pylint calls it bare-except.

title: Catching previously caught exception type ….
summary: Used when an except catches a type that was already caught by a previous handler. pylint calls it duplicate-except.

title: The except handler raises immediately.
summary: Used when an except handler uses raise as its first or only operator. This is useless because it raises back the exception immediately. Remove the raise operator or the entire try-except-raise block!. pylint calls it try-except-raise.

title: Consider explicitly re-raising using …'… from …'.
summary: Python's exception chaining shows the traceback of the current exception, but also of the original exception. When you raise a new exception after another exception was caught it's likely that the second exception is a friendly re-wrapping of the first exception. In such cases raise from provides a better link between the two tracebacks in the final error. pylint calls it raise-missing-from.

title: Exception to catch is the result of a binary "…" operation.
summary: Used when the exception to catch is of the form "except A or B:". If intending to catch multiple, rewrite as "except (A, B):". pylint calls it binary-op-exception.
message_templates: Exception to catch is the result of a binary "{}" operation

title: Exception arguments suggest string formatting might be intended.
summary: Used when passing multiple arguments to an exception constructor, the first of them a string literal containing what appears to be placeholders intended for formatting. pylint calls it raising-format-tuple.
message_templates: Exception arguments suggest string formatting might be intended

title: Invalid exception operation. ….
summary: Used when an operation is done against an exception, but the operation is not valid for the exception in question. Usually emitted when having binary operations between exceptions in except handlers. pylint calls it wrong-exception-operation.

title: Catching too general exception ….
summary: If you use a naked except Exception: clause, you might end up catching exceptions other than the ones you expect to catch. This can hide bugs or make it harder to debug programs when unrelated errors are hidden. pylint calls it broad-exception-caught.

title: Raising too general exception: ….
summary: Raising exceptions that are too generic force you to catch exceptions generically too. It will force you to use a naked except Exception: clause. You might then end up catching exceptions other than the ones you expect to catch. This can hide bugs or make it harder to debug programs when unrelated errors are hidden. pylint calls it broad-exception-raised.
